textbookBox.concept: Electric current is the rate of flow of charge: I = Q/t. Its unit is the ampere (A), measured by an ammeter connected in series.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Electric current is the rate of flow of charge: I = Q/t. Its unit is the ampere (A), measured by an ammeter connected in series.
beats.speakEn: Electric current is the rate of flow of charge: I  equals  Q/t. Its unit is the ampere (A), measured by an ammeter connected in series.

beats.en: Conventional current flows from positive to negative terminal; electrons flow the other way.

textbookBox.concept: Potential difference is the work done to move a unit charge: V = W/Q, in volts, measured by a voltmeter connected in parallel.

beats.en: Potential difference is the work done to move a unit charge: V = W/Q, in volts, measured by a voltmeter connected in parallel.
beats.speakEn: Potential difference is the work done to move a unit charge: V  equals  W/Q, in volts, measured by a voltmeter connected in parallel.

beats.en: Ohm's law: at constant temperature, the current through a conductor is proportional to the potential difference, V = IR.
beats.speakEn: Ohm's law: at constant temperature, the current through a conductor is proportional to the potential difference, V  equals  IR.
